question: Can the historical Binance USD-M perpetual archive support a reproducible daily point-in-time shortable universe using only completed information, while preserving later-ended contracts historically?
candidate_source: TSMOM-DATA-0027 ordinary USDT perpetual archive universe

frozen_eligibility_rule.effective_for_trading: eligibility observed at completed UTC day t is usable no earlier than t+1
frozen_eligibility_rule.post_contract_end: ineligible naturally because no completed bar exists
frozen_eligibility_rule.symbol_exclusions: reuse TSMOM-DATA-0027 mechanical stable-base and leveraged-token-like exclusions

parameter_provenance.240_days: exact existing PIT-DISP-0015 minimum contiguous-history rule
parameter_provenance.25m_quote_volume: exact existing PIT-DISP-0015 completed-day quote-volume floor
parameter_provenance.note: No TSMOM PNL or future returns are used to choose either value.

required_outputs: per-symbol first/last archive date and first/last eligible date
historical ended-contracts that were previously eligible
selected calendar snapshots of eligible symbols
proof that no eligibility occurs before 240 contiguous bars
success_gate: historical ordinary perpetual candidates remain nonempty
daily archive histories can be resolved with no material systematic gaps
a nontrivial daily eligible universe exists
at least one later-ended historical contract is shown to have been eligible before its history ended
eligibility construction uses only same-day-or-earlier completed data
prohibited: no liquidity or age threshold search
no future return or later delisting information in daily eligibility
no asset ranking or Top-K selection
stopping_rule: If the PIT eligibility layer passes, the next experiment may preregister a TSMOM signal/risk-normalization specification. If it fails, repair data completeness only; do not calculate strategy PNL from a compromised universe.
